You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

+
+## Task-specific pattern: segmented border rays
+
+When a grid has a uniform field, a border color forming one or more contiguous edge segments, and isolated colored pixels inside those segments:
+
+- A marker (e.g. color 2) aligned along the row of a vertical border segment extends horizontally away from that border to the marker's column. Fill the intervening uniform cells with the marker color, preserve the border, and recolor the marker cell to 4 (the ray's origin cap).
+- On the other hand, a marker in a horizontal border segment extends vertically inward from that border to the marker's row, in the same manner: intervening field cells become marker color, with the marker changed to 4.
+- The border segments themselves remain unchanged. Do not fill the entire row/column; rays only span between the relevant border and marker. Leave unrelated rows/cells untouched.
+- Determine orientation from which edge segment and axis correspond, not from presumed inside direction. Validate on examples: in the successful task-679ab180 test, left-edge segment rows 12-22 had markers on rows 14,18,22; each ray filled from col 1 through marker col, with marker recolored 4. The first two guesses were wrong because they extended rays in the wrong direction / filled unsupported rows. A correct working rule filled only marker rows.
+- Other demos showed the same operation: horizontal border segments at row 0 / row 4 lead to vertical rays; vertical border segments at right/left edges lead to horizontal rays. Color 4 marks the marker pixel; color 2 fills ray path. Ray starts adjacent to border, leaving border intact.
+
+Use a demo to disambiguate ray orientation if test topology is unclear; do not infer extra rays from borders alone. Note a previous mistaken output added full rows without corresponding seeds; avoid that.
*** End Patch
